title: Go: Task Orchestrator
description: Build a DAG-based task orchestrator with topological sorting, parallel goroutine execution, error propagation, and retry logic.

steps.title: Task and DAG structs
steps.description: Define `Task` with `ID string`, `Run func() error`, and `DependsOn []string` (task IDs). Define `DAG` with `Tasks map[string]*Task`. Implement `NewDAG() *DAG` and `AddTask(t *Task) error`. Print the number of registered tasks with `fmt.Println(len(dag.Tasks))`.
hints: Use `map[string]*Task` for O(1) lookup by ID.
`AddTask` checks for duplicate IDs and returns an error if found.
Initialize the map in the constructor.

verification.failureMessage: AddTask should add a task and increment the task count.

steps.title: Dependency graph construction
steps.description: Enhance `AddTask` to validate that all `DependsOn` references exist. Implement `GetDependencies(taskID string) []string` and `GetDependents(taskID string) []string` by building a reverse edge map. Print the dependents of a root task.
hints: Build `reverse map[string][]string` (dependent → dependency).
Also build `dependents map[string][]string` (dependency → dependent).
Validate dependencies exist in `AddTask` before adding.

verification.failureMessage: Dependents should list all tasks that depend on a given task.

steps.title: Kahn's topological sort
steps.description: Implement `TopologicalSort() ([]string, error)` using Kahn's algorithm. Compute in-degree for each task, start with zero-in-degree nodes, process in order. Return an error if a cycle is detected. Print the sorted task IDs with `fmt.Println(order)`.
hints: Track in-degree in `map[string]int`.
Use a queue (slice) for zero-in-degree tasks.
If processed count != total tasks, there's a cycle.

verification.successMessage: Topological sort produces a valid order.
verification.failureMessage: Sort should return tasks in dependency order; error on cycles.

steps.title: Parallel execution with goroutines
steps.description: Implement `Execute() error` that runs tasks in parallel respecting dependencies. Use channels to signal task completion. When a task finishes, check if any dependent tasks have all dependencies satisfied and launch them. Print `"task X done"` as each completes using `fmt.Printf("task %s done\n", taskID)`.
hints: Track `completed map[string]bool`.
Use `sync.WaitGroup` or a channel-based approach to wait for tasks.
A dispatcher goroutine checks which tasks are ready to run.

verification.successMessage: Tasks execute in correct dependency order.
verification.failureMessage: Each task should print 'done' as it completes.

steps.title: Error propagation
steps.description: If any task's `Run()` returns an error, cancel all pending downstream tasks and propagate the error. Implement a cancellation context. Print `"task X failed: <error>"` and stop execution immediately without running dependents.
hints: Pass `context.Context` to Execute.
Use `context.WithCancel` to propagate cancellation.
Goroutines check `ctx.Done()` before starting new tasks.

verification.successMessage: Errors propagate and cancel downstream tasks.
verification.failureMessage: A failing task should cancel all dependents and return the error.

steps.title: Retry logic
steps.description: Add `MaxRetries int` to `Task`. If a task fails and `MaxRetries > 0`, retry up to that many times with exponential backoff. Print `"retrying task X (attempt N)"` on each retry using `fmt.Printf("retrying %s attempt %d\n", task.ID, attempt)`.
hints: Wrap `Run()` in a retry loop with `time.Sleep(backoff)` between attempts.
Exponential backoff: `time.Duration(math.Pow(2, float64(attempt))) * time.Second`.
Only retry if `attempt < task.MaxRetries`; otherwise propagate the error.

verification.failureMessage: A task with MaxRetries > 0 should retry on failure.

steps.title: Execution report
steps.description: After `Execute()` completes (or fails), generate an `ExecutionReport` with task ID, duration, status (success/failed/skipped), and error. Print the report using `fmt.Printf("%s: %s (%v)", r.TaskID, r.Status, r.Duration)` for each task.
hints: Track `startTime` and `endTime` for each task execution.
`ExecutionReport` is a slice of `TaskResult` structs.
Skipped tasks (due to upstream failure) have status `"skipped"`.

verification.successMessage: Execution report contains status for all tasks.
verification.failureMessage: Every registered task should have an entry in the execution report.
